lesson.parent_notes:
Parent: Marking guidance for the independent task: Handwrite a final page or section of your report. Check layout criteria and keep it as evidence. Accept equivalent original responses that show the same skill.

Parent: Written model 1: Original response on new material: Headings clear; spacing; arm’s-length legibility. Reasoning: I used final copy by attending to handwriting rather than copying the worked model.

Parent: Written model 2: Common error: Illegible fancy script hides good research. Correction: Headings clear; spacing; arm’s-length legibility. Why: the correction restores accurate use of final copy.

Parent: Likely misconception: Illegible fancy script hides good research. Keep sample answers out of the child role.

Parent: Short-answer focus 1: Produce a fresh example demonstrating final copy on new material (not the worked model). Explain the particular words, sources or choices that make it work.

Parent: Short-answer focus 2: Name one likely error with final copy, correct it, and explain why the correction helps a reader or audience.

teach_steps.explain:
Handwriting a final copy means legible letters, clear headings and spacing so a reader can use the report without decoding struggle.

WHY IT MATTERS
This helps the learner make decisions based on specific language evidence, rather than guess or copy someone else. Keep the meaning accurate and explain the choice.

HOW TO WORK
Read the original example and locate the words or actions that support the idea. Before looking at the correction, make your own attempt using the exact question provided. Check your response against the feedback: did you address the same skill and show your reasoning? If a detail is uncertain, identify what would have to be checked. One deliberate, justified revision is more useful than making the answer longer.
